incidents.vector: Ransomware intrusion that encrypted IT systems and forced two sugar mills offline shortly after the cane-crushing season began.
incidents.impact: Australia's second-largest sugar producer had its Racecourse and Farleigh mills shut since June 10; the Gentlemen group claims data theft and threatens to leak it, while the company restores systems and verifies the breach.

incidents.victim: Open-source software ecosystem (npm, PyPI, GitHub, RubyGems)
incidents.vector: Compromise of maintainer credentials and CI/CD runners to inject credential-stealing malware into packages, with a self-replicating worm spreading across registries.
incidents.impact: In under four months TeamPCP poisoned 1,000+ packages (claimed victims include SAP, Red Hat, GitHub, Mistral AI, Bitwarden); researchers count 516 live malicious packages, 3,000+ affected repos and 200+ compromised developer accounts. GitHub dismissed two related vulnerability reports.

incidents.vector: Initial access via an exposed high-privileged GitHub personal access token in client-side JavaScript, then cloning of private repos and harvesting of further credentials to pivot across the network.
incidents.impact: Attackers spent two-plus months inside, exfiltrating ~1.3TB (700k+ files) including source code, drug research, internal AI models and ~11,500 clinical-trial participants' pseudonymized data; a $25M ransom was refused and data is now being leaked. A second group (TheUSERS007) also claims a separate intrusion.

incidents.vector: Multinational law-enforcement takedown (Operation Endgame/Riptide) of malware that compromised WordPress sites and used traffic-distribution systems to push malware and ransomware.
incidents.impact: Authorities from the US, Canada, Germany, the Netherlands and Europol seized 106 servers and remediated nearly 15,000 infected sites, disabling a botnet that provided initial access for LockBit, RansomHub, DoppelPaymer and others since 2017.

incidents.vector: Network intrusion and data theft, surfaced when the group listed Kodak on its dark-web leak site.
incidents.impact: ShinyHunters claims theft of details on nearly 2.2 million customers; Kodak confirmed unauthorized network access but has not detailed the scope.

incidents.vector: Breach of the agency's hunting/fishing license registration website.
incidents.impact: Personal details of more than three million people were stolen, including highly sensitive government IDs, driver's licenses and home addresses; the breach date was not disclosed.

incidents.vector: Exploitation of legacy smart contracts and deprecated components that were never decommissioned.
incidents.impact: Aztec Connect was drained twice in a week ($2.1M then $2M); Raydium lost $1.34M and DxSale was also hit in what researchers describe as a coordinated campaign against legacy contracts.

incidents.victim: Consumer Android TV boxes (Popa / Vo1d botnet)
incidents.attacker: Criminal — proxy and ad-fraud botnet (linked to NetNut/Alarum)
incidents.vector: Malicious SDK pre-installed on unofficial Android TV boxes enrolls home devices into a residential-proxy pool, often without user consent.
incidents.impact: Researchers tie the 1.5-2.5M-IP/day Popa botnet to publicly-traded Israeli proxy firm NetNut/Alarum; infected devices relay traffic used for ad fraud, account takeovers and mass data-scraping. Alarum disputes the 'botnet' characterization.

incidents.victim: Salesforce customers via Klue 'Battlecards' app (incl. Huntress)
incidents.vector: Compromise of Klue's market-intelligence backend via a long-disused but active credential, then theft of customer OAuth tokens to reach connected Salesforce instances and bulk-export data via the REST API.
incidents.impact: Third confirmed third-party-app OAuth abuse against Salesforce (after Salesloft Drift and Gainsight); attackers ran ~1,000 queries in 15 minutes and sustained six-plus hours of exfiltration. Huntress confirmed theft of sales contacts and quotes; Icarus warns 'big corps' will be listed.

incidents.vector: Active exploitation of Fortinet FortiSandbox flaws CVE-2026-39808 (OS-command injection) and CVE-2026-39813 (path traversal), disclosed in April, plus attempts on CVE-2026-25089.
incidents.impact: Researchers observed 49 exploitation events from 11 IPs over six days across nine countries; post-exploitation reconnaissance against trusted sandbox appliances typically precedes a heavier attack wave. Fortinet has not confirmed exploitation and the CVEs are not yet in CISA's KEV catalog.

incidents.vector: Takeover of the 'ehindero' maintainer account to publish 140+ poisoned packages injected with 'easy-day-js,' a typosquat of dayjs whose postinstall hook ran an obfuscated dropper, disabled TLS verification and fetched a second-stage tasking implant.
incidents.impact: Any developer or CI/CD pipeline running npm install after the compromise risked credential, token and build-environment theft; the implant enabled persistent remote code execution. npm removed the packages and revoked the attacker's publish access.

incidents.vector: Malicious USB-borne .lnk shortcuts deploy a worm and a script-based clipper that launches a bundled Tor proxy, polls a hidden-service C2, and monitors the clipboard for wallet data.
incidents.impact: Active since February 2026, the malware steals BIP39 seed phrases and private keys, exfiltrates screenshots over Tor, swaps copied wallet addresses for attacker-controlled ones, and can execute arbitrary code via an EVAL command, turning a stealer into a lightweight backdoor.

incidents.vector: Chinese police arrested 67 suspects who spread the Silver Fox/Winos trojan via malspam and fake download/app sites to deploy infostealers and custom RATs.
incidents.impact: Arrests across five provinces dismantled China's largest domestic cybercrime operation, including the trojan's author Ji Moufei; the group had recently begun expanding beyond Chinese-speaking targets.

incidents.vector: Fully automated credential reuse, stuffing and password spraying against exposed Fortinet management and VPN interfaces using credentials leaked in prior breaches; compromised devices then harvest fresh credentials passing through them.
incidents.impact: SOCRadar's 'FortiBleed' research found a verified repository of working logins for 30,791 devices (21,108 IPs, 8,316 domains) across government, telecom, healthcare and critical infrastructure; targeting was NATO-weighted and included a defense-industry VPN, suggesting espionage alongside financial motives.

incidents.victim: Iranian banks (Bank Melli, Tejarat, Saderat, EDBI)
incidents.vector: Cyberattack reportedly targeting communications infrastructure shared by four of Iran's largest banks.
incidents.impact: Online portals and mobile apps for Bank Melli, Bank Tejarat, Bank Saderat and the Export Development Bank of Iran were down over the weekend; the banking council said no customer data was accessed. Occurred amid the Iran War context.

incidents.vector: Client-side-only authorization in FIFA's Microsoft Entra environment: a self-registered football-agent account passed the backend API, which enforced no server-side access control.
incidents.impact: Researcher 'BobDaHacker' gained control of World Cup broadcast streaming, match-management, commentary and analytics platforms — able to black out or replace global TV feeds and alter scores. Reported via CISA/FBI (FIFA had no disclosure channel) and fixed the next day; no malicious exploitation observed.

incidents.vector: Law-enforcement outcome: Ukrainian national Oleksii Lytvynenko pleaded guilty after extradition from Ireland for conspiring to deploy Conti ransomware and code a malware 'loader.'
incidents.impact: Conti infected 1,000+ networks across 47 US states and 31 countries (2020-2022), causing at least $150M in ransom payments; Lytvynenko faces up to 20 years, sentencing Sept. 10, 2026.

incidents.vector: Network of 13 fake 'consulting' company websites and job postings using AI-generated photos, stolen identities and encrypted apps to lure current and former clearance holders into selling sensitive information.
incidents.impact: DOJ and FBI seized the 13 domains used to recruit Americans with access to classified information; the FBI assessed the operation as backed by Chinese intelligence services and placed takeover notices on the sites.

incidents.victim: Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS / GlobalProtect operators
incidents.vector: Active exploitation of CVE-2026-0257, an authentication-bypass flaw in PAN-OS GlobalProtect portal and gateway components, allowing unauthorized VPN connections.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 observed an unidentified actor probing and, in a small number of cases, establishing GlobalProtect VPN sessions; the CVE was added to CISA's KEV catalog on May 29 and no post-access lateral movement has yet been confirmed.
